CONFIRMED FIXED: with the member detached from every project, POST /orgs/{org}/tasks -> 403, POST /orgs/{org}/sprints -> 403, GET /orgs/{org}/time-entries -> [] (also projects/tasks/sprints [], analytics total_tasks=0, PATCH/DELETE task 403, task comments GET/POST 403, project-members roster 403, PATCH project 403). After re-attaching to 'Web Redesign': 1 project / 5 tasks visible, GET /time-entries returns 4 entries all scoped to accessible tasks with no _id leak, POST /sprints still 403 (manager+ role check), project roster 200, comments 200, duplicate member add -> 400 'Already a project member'. critical.issue: NEW GAP (same class as the 3 just fixed): only calls ensure_member(). A member detached from every project successfully logged 7 minutes on a task inside an inaccessible project (200) and it incremented that task's logged_minutes. Should call require_task_access(org_id, body.task_id, user) (and validate the task exists in the org).

minor.issue: No role check: an attached role='member' creates tasks successfully (200). The review request states this should be 403 unless promoted, and the UI hides 'New task' for members (canCreate = owner/admin/manager), so backend and frontend disagree. Decide the intended rule; if members may create tasks in their own projects, the UI guard should be relaxed instead.

project_id is only a str — the seeded/legacy task 'Bug fix test' has project_id='' so it renders as '—' and is invisible to every non-admin (orphan). Validate that the project exists in the org before insert.
Still 200 {'ok': true} when nothing was deleted (deleted_count == 0). Unchanged from iterations 6-7.

Still no DELETE /orgs/{org}/projects/{id}; I removed leftover TEST_Project / TEST_AutoLead straight from MongoDB again this iteration. Also 8+ leftover QA users named 'TEST_RegularMember' remain as org members.

Testid is 'comment-submit-btn' while every other add action uses 'add-*-btn' (e.g. add-project-member-btn) — naming inconsistency only, works fine.

action_items: HIGH: Apply require_task_access() to POST /orgs/{org}/time-entries — a project-less member can still log time on tasks they cannot see (and mutate logged_minutes).
MEDIUM: Decide and align the create-task rule: either add a manager+ role check to POST /orgs/{org}/tasks (matches the UI's canCreate guard and the review request) or relax the UI guard for members.
LOW: Validate body.project_id points to an existing project in the org on task/sprint create (the 'Bug fix test' task has project_id='' and shows as '—').

LOW: Update the Tasks empty-state copy for members; add DELETE /orgs/{org}/projects/{id}; return 404 from DELETE project-member when nothing was deleted; give /analytics its own heading or drop the duplicate route.
critical_code_review_comments: The require_project_access()/require_task_access() helpers are now applied to create_task, create_sprint, update/delete task and comments, but POST /time-entries was missed — this is the 4th route in the same class. Convert the check into a FastAPI dependency (e.g. Depends(project_access) / Depends(task_access)) so no future body-driven write path can forget it.

Role checks are inconsistent between sibling write routes: create_sprint and create_project require manager+, create_task and create_time_entry require nothing. Centralise a require_role(min_role) helper.
server.py is still 1166 lines; split into auth / orgs+projects / tasks+time / analytics / email-cron routers.
analytics() still reuses the local name `m` for both the membership doc and the per-day minutes sum (~line 859).

rca_of_the_issue: Iteration 7's three gaps are genuinely closed: create_task and create_sprint now call require_project_access(org_id, body.project_id, user) (create_sprint additionally requires manager+), and list_time_entries resolves the accessible project ids -> accessible task ids and filters time_entries by task_id. The residual defect has the identical root cause on the one write path that was not audited: create_time_entry still authorizes with ensure_member(org_id, user_id) only and never validates body.task_id, so a member with 0 project memberships can POST a time entry against any task in the org (verified 200, and tasks.logged_minutes is incremented). Reproduction: (1) owner DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/projects/{prj}/members/{member_uid}; (2) member POST /api/orgs/{org}/time-entries {"task_id":"<task in prj>","minutes":7} -> 200. Mitigation: await require_task_access(org_id, body.task_id, user) at the top of create_time_entry.
